newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes rise with WTI, tight discount.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes rise with WTI, tight discount.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes rose Friday with firmer West Texas Intermediate (WTI) values and tightening discounts for heavy grades, players said.
No light crudes traded Friday and players doubted cargoes would move next week with many traders attending an annual refinery conference in Texas.
Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, a western benchmark, traded at -$0.91 cents under April WTI Thursday. The cargo, confirmed by both sides, lowered the discount 11 cents from Wednesday.
ANS crude ranged $20.29/20.49 a barrel, up 65 cents.
Two shipments of San Joaquin Valley heavy (SJV) grade sold for 20 cents under postings late this week, one Thursday and one Friday, a seller confirmed.
"I think (heavies) will strengthen in the next week or so," a seller said.
The shipments contain several thousand barrels per day for April delivery, according to trader sources. The minus 20-cent price raises the discount market from a 45-cent level seen last month.
Outright prices for Kern River, a representative heavy grade, rose 13 cents to $14.38/14.48 a barrel, because of the tighter discount and increase in Texaco's posted prices.
Line 63 stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05.
